narrative.overview: A quiet library table at the end of the day: warm paper, dark ink, a lamp's worth of soft shadow, and one red seal. Umbrella is a product about reading, so its interface behaves like a well-set page.
keyCharacteristics: Paper-toned backgrounds, ink-toned text; no pure white, no pure black.
Serif for voice (display and body), sans-serif (Inter) only for functional UI.
Soft, warm, brown-tinted shadows; surfaces feel like paper laid on paper.
Generous reading rhythm: 1.75 body line height, 16px base.

rules.name: The Red Seal Rule
rules.body: Vermilion appears on a small share of any screen: the primary action, the wordmark, one emphasized phrase.

rules.name: The Warm Neutral Rule
rules.body: Every neutral leans warm. Never introduce a cool gray or pure white/black.

rules.name: The Serif Voice Rule
rules.body: Reading content and headlines are serif. Inter is reserved for controls.

rules.name: The Brown Shadow Rule
rules.body: Shadows are warm and low-contrast. A gray or black shadow breaks the paper illusion.

dos: Do keep every surface and text color inside the paper and ink families, with vermilion as the single accent.
Do set headlines in Crimson Pro and reading text in Source Serif 4; use Inter only for controls.
Do use ink-brown tinted shadows and lift them on hover.
Do use deep vermilion (#C0392B), not bright, for vermilion text on paper.
Do keep body line height at 1.75 and paragraphs to 65 to 75ch.
donts: Don't use pure white, pure black, or cool grays.
Don't use vermilion for more than one competing focal point per screen.
Don't use sharp corners or pill shapes; stay in the 12 to 24px radius range.
Don't use gray or black drop shadows.
Don't treat the dark-mode block as real: it maps to the same light values.
Don't introduce the teal palette from design-tokens.ts and the PRD; the shipped site is vermilion-only.
